gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho reads chunky, like chalk pressed hard onto a board. Starborn floats above it with wide gaps and a dark lowercase stripe, so the heavy plain sans body grounds the dreamy heading.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square reads approachable, its wide gaps keeping tiny sizes crisp while a soaring x-height lifts every line. Starborn adds a dreamy, widely spaced heading with a dark lowercase stripe.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-numans: Starborn scatters huge gaps between its letters, then lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line. But Numans, the plain sans below, holds the text with swollen lowercase and tracking pushed well past normal.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-onest: Starborn is all drifting space and one dark lowercase stripe. Onest, a sans-serif with short ascenders over big bowls, would read smoothly down the page, its curves never pinching or pooling.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-open-sans: Dreamy, gappy, dark-striped: that's Starborn up top. Open Sans comes in with bulky lowercase proportions and curves that never clog, so the reading feels smooth all the way down.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-orienta: Starborn hangs its dark lowercase in wide, drifting space. Orienta reads modern and level down the page, its open counters breathing and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-oxygen: Starborn's thick, dark stripe of lowercase runs through every line, with wide gaps between the letters. Oxygen reads cleanly over many lines, since its curves stay open and its lowercase nearly matches the capitals.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme keeps stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height. Its best trick is the push and pull, with Starborn drifting dreamy and spaced out while rounded letters stay clearly open.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-preahvihear: Dreamy first: Starborn drifts through wide gaps and a dark lowercase stripe. Preahvihear does the grounded work, its open letter mouths and lofty x-height keeping the sans-serif text easy going.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-puritan: Puritan is rounded and open, with oversized e and a counters. Starborn does its best work as the dreamy, widely spaced heading, while the sans handles the text with clear, friendly forms.
